newsitem.title: INDIA: India crash victim dies near his own village.
newsitem.headline: India crash victim dies near his own village.

text.p: Bajinder Singh left his village in northern India on Tuesday to fly to Saudi Arabia.
Six hours later he was lying dead among the wreckage of a 747 jumbo jet, strewn across fields not far from Talao, the village where he lived.
Rajinder Singh, who went with his brother to New Delhi to see him off on the Saudi Arabian Airlines flight, learned of Bajinder's death when he got home from the airport and turned on the television.
His brother's flight to Dhahran and Jeddah had ended in the world's worst mid-air collision that left about 350 people dead.
On Wednesday morning Rajinder was at the crash site, 100 km (60 miles) southwest of Talao, to identify his brother's charred body.
"I never knew I would have to come back to identify his body," a shaken Rajinder said. "In fact he had invited me to Jeddah but now he has gone away."
Bajinder, 25, had returned to India from Jeddah where he worked as an artisan to celebrate the Hindu festive season with his family. He was due back in Saudi Arabia on Wednesday.
"Talao will be poorer without Bajinder," said his uncle Gulab, who had also accompanied Bajinder to New Delhi and then helped identify his body.
"He had been helping the people of the village by sending them money," he said.
Many of the passengers on the Saudi Arabian Airlines flight were Indians returning to jobs in the Gulf.
